title: Finite Relational Adapter Controlled Empirical Pilot V0
run_context: controlled synthetic finite-substrate study generated by omega.validation.finite_relational_adapter_empirical
claim_boundary: Synthetic finite adapter empirics over declared small search spaces. This measures how often selected proxy summaries fail within toy finite families. It does not validate a real substrate, prove alignment, infer value, establish agency, or validate Omega.

families.question: Does a fixed 2/2 observation histogram determine bounded target recoverability?
Does an unordered bag summary determine an order-sensitive trace target?
How often can a stale abstract transition hide exact reachability loss in the declared three-state search space?
Does endpoint safety plus forward reachability determine recurrent carrier certification?

interpretation: This is the first controlled finite empirical pilot, not external validation.
The study moves beyond single hand-written fixtures by enumerating declared small families.
Each family retains representative generic audit cases with digests in the run output.
The results support the adapter discipline: proxy summaries and weaker continuation facts need target-specific audits.
